reference.source: Primer on the Metabolic Bone Diseases / Williams Textbook of Endocrinology
clinicalPearls: A recessively inherited FGF23-mediated phosphate-wasting disorder caused by loss-of-function mutations in DMP1 (ARHR1) or ENPP1 (ARHR2)
Both genes normally restrain osteocyte FGF23 production, so their loss leads to excess circulating FGF23 and the familiar phosphaturic biochemical picture
Presents with rickets, short stature, bowing, and bone pain in children and osteomalacia in adults, similar to X-linked and autosomal dominant forms
Biochemistry shows hypophosphataemia, renal phosphate wasting, and inappropriately low or normal 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D with normal calcium and parathyroid hormone
ENPP1 loss also reduces pyrophosphate and is associated with generalised arterial calcification of infancy, so cardiovascular assessment matters in ARHR2
Because it is recessive, a family history may be absent, and consanguinity increases risk
Treatment follows the FGF23-driven paradigm with oral phosphate salts and active vitamin D, or FGF23-directed antibody therapy where available
reference.pathophysiology: Dentin matrix protein 1 (DMP1) and ectonucleotide pyrophosphatase/phosphodiesterase 1 (ENPP1) are expressed by osteocytes and normally suppress FGF23 synthesis. Biallelic loss-of-function mutations release this brake, so osteocytes overproduce FGF23. Elevated FGF23 drives renal phosphate wasting through downregulation of proximal sodium-phosphate cotransporters and suppresses 1-alpha-hydroxylase, leaving 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D inappropriately low. Chronic hypophosphataemia impairs skeletal mineralisation, producing rickets and osteomalacia. In ARHR2, ENPP1 deficiency additionally lowers extracellular pyrophosphate, an inhibitor of ectopic mineralisation, which paradoxically predisposes to arterial and periarticular calcification alongside the phosphate-wasting bone disease.
additionalDifferentials: Generalised arterial calcification of infancy from other causes
additionalInvestigations: Serum phosphate with tubular reabsorption indices confirming renal wasting
Calcium, parathyroid hormone, alkaline phosphatase, and 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D
Radiographs for rachitic changes and, in suspected ENPP1 disease, vascular imaging for arterial calcification
Cardiovascular evaluation in ARHR2 given the risk of arterial calcification of infancy
Sequencing of DMP1 and ENPP1 to establish the specific genotype
redFlags: Signs of arterial calcification or cardiovascular compromise in an infant with ENPP1 disease
Severe progressive skeletal deformity or growth failure
Enthesopathy and joint stiffness limiting mobility
Nephrocalcinosis or hyperparathyroidism emerging on therapy
reference.prognosis: Skeletal outcome with phosphate and active vitamin D therapy resembles other FGF23-driven rickets, but ARHR2 carries an added burden from ENPP1-related vascular calcification that can dominate the prognosis and requires dedicated cardiovascular follow-up.
pitfalls: Overlooking the recessive inheritance when there is no affected parent
Missing arterial calcification in ENPP1 deficiency by focusing only on the bone disease
Failing to distinguish ARHR from X-linked disease, altering genetic counselling
Inducing nephrocalcinosis and secondary hyperparathyroidism with unmonitored conventional therapy
references: Primer on the Metabolic Bone Diseases and Disorders of Mineral Metabolism
management: Replace with oral phosphate salts and an active vitamin D analogue such as calcitriol or alfacalcidol to heal the rickets and osteomalacia
Consider the anti-FGF23 monoclonal antibody burosumab as targeted therapy where conventional replacement is insufficient
In ENPP1-related ARHR2 arrange cardiovascular assessment and surveillance for arterial calcification, with emerging ENPP1 enzyme replacement under specialist care
Monitor phosphate, calcium, alkaline phosphatase and parathyroid hormone, with renal ultrasound for nephrocalcinosis and vigilance for tertiary hyperparathyroidism
Treat limb deformity with orthopaedic review and physiotherapy, and provide dental surveillance for spontaneous abscesses
Offer genetic counselling and family screening, noting recessive inheritance and heightened risk with consanguinity
Manage through a metabolic bone service with nephrology and, in ARHR2, cardiology input
